transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the release package review for 'After the Flood' ahead of the Meridian International Film Festival. I'll need each of you — rights, music, publicity, and accessibility — to walk me through your respective reviews so we can address any issues before I lock the package. I have the current draft release sheet in front of me: worldwide access, the cue 'Low Tide,' the working title 'River After Rain,' and optional accessibility materials. Who'd like to begin?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical rights issue. I confirmed with the archive this week that the license for our archival interview permits festival screening and password-protected press access only in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland. It forbids public online access and access in all other territories. The archive's signed email arrived after the last package revision, so I haven't yet copied the confirmation into the release sheet. This directly conflicts with the current draft listing worldwide access.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a music clearance issue. I confirmed with the publisher that the current cue 'Low Tide' is only cleared for 30 seconds, but our trailer segment runs 46 seconds. The good news is that the alternate cue 'Northbound' is fully cleared for the entire 46-second segment. I haven't updated the cue name in the package yet because the editor delivered the latest cut after my clearance check, so the sheet still lists 'Low Tide.' We need to replace it with 'Northbound' before the package is locked.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a publicity issue to flag. I'm holding the filmmaker's signed publicity approval, which requires the title 'After the Flood' and the credit line 'A film by Nia Okafor.' The draft release sheet still lists the working title 'River After Rain' and a generic credit because the signed approval arrived during the poster revision and I haven't updated the sheet yet. We need to correct both the title and the credit line before the package is locked.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical accessibility issue. I confirmed with the festival's access coordinator that the final submission must include open English captions and a separate audio-description track. The coordinator will reject a package containing either deliverable as optional. This requirement came through a separate accessibility email, so I haven't yet updated the release checklist — but the current draft listing accessibility materials as optional will not pass festival ingest.
transcript.speaker: A5
